blocks.text: The daily grind of grant administration

Grant administrators spend much of their day in a state of constant context switching. You move from budget spreadsheets to donor emails and then to compliance reports. Your inbox is where most of these threads converge. When you use Outlook for nonprofit grant administrators on Mac, you are likely managing multiple grant cycles at once. This requires a high level of organization.

Many administrators struggle with the sheer volume of incoming requests. You need to keep track of deadlines, donor inquiries, and internal updates. If your email is cluttered, you risk missing a critical communication from a program officer or a funder. The goal is to spend less time managing the inbox and more time securing funding for your mission.
Managing your inbox effectively

Start by cleaning up your view. If you feel overwhelmed, turn off the Focused Inbox to see all your mail in one place. Go to View > Focused Inbox to toggle this setting. This ensures you do not miss emails that are filtered into the Other tab by mistake.

Use folders to categorize your grants. Right-click your inbox and select New Folder to create a system that works for you. You might organize by grant cycle, donor, or department. This helps you keep track of specific documentation related to each project.

items: Create a folder for each active grant project.
Use rules to move incoming emails from specific funders into their folders.
Pin important emails that require follow-up later in the day.
Set reminders for emails that need a reply by a specific deadline.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts for speed

Efficiency comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Use ⌘ + 1 to switch to Mail, ⌘ + 2 for Calendar, and ⌘ + 3 for Contacts. These shortcuts save seconds every time you switch views. Over a day, these seconds add up to minutes of saved time.

If you want to create a new email, press ⌘ + N. When you are ready to send, press ⌘ + Return. These are standard, but they are the foundation of a fast workflow. You can also customize your own shortcuts in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts if you find yourself using a specific menu item often.
Common Outlook issues for Mac users

Syncing is a common pain point. If you see error -3253, it means your connection to the server was dropped. Check your internet connection first. If it persists, restart Outlook. If you are using the new Outlook interface, check the Outlook menu to see if you have any pending updates. Microsoft updates the app frequently to fix these bugs.

Search can also be slow. If you are struggling to find an old grant report, use the search bar at the top with filters. Click the filter icon to search by sender, date, or folder. This is much faster than scrolling through your inbox.
Staying organized with Lazur

Lazur is a voice assistant that helps you work faster in Outlook. When you hold ⌥ ⌘, you can ask where a button is or how to perform a task. Lazur will point at the screen to show you the way. This is useful when you are in a hurry and cannot remember where a specific setting is hidden.

You can also use the fn key to dictate emails. If you are drafting a long donor update, just hold the key and speak. Lazur will type your words at the cursor. This is a great way to get your thoughts down without needing to type everything manually.
Preparing for audits

Audit trails are vital for grant administrators. Keep your correspondence organized by date and subject. If you need to export your emails for an audit, use the File > Export menu. Note that the new Outlook interface handles exports differently than the legacy version. Always keep a backup of your important grant communications in a separate folder or on a secure server.
Customizing your signature

Your email signature should include your title and links to your organization's website. Go to Outlook > Settings > Signatures to create one. Keep it simple and professional. Avoid large images that might be blocked by some email servers.
Managing shared mailboxes

If your nonprofit uses a shared mailbox for grant inquiries, add it to your Outlook account. Go to File > Open > Shared Mailbox. This allows you to monitor incoming messages without needing to log in and out of different accounts. It is a vital tool for team collaboration.
Setting up automatic replies

When you are away from your desk, set an automatic reply. Go to Tools > Automatic Replies. Make sure to include a contact person in case of an emergency. This manages expectations for donors and partners while you are out.
Best practices for grant communication

items: Always proofread your emails before sending.
Use clear subject lines that include the grant name.
Keep emails brief and to the point.
Attach all necessary files before hitting send.
Follow up on sent emails if you do not receive a response within a week.

blocks.text: Taking the next steps

Take time to learn your tools. Read the Microsoft support documentation for your version of Outlook. Explore the settings menu to see what you can customize. By investing time in your setup now, you will save time on every grant you manage in the future.

faq.question: How do I switch between the new and legacy Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: You can toggle the experience using the Outlook menu in the menu bar. Look for the option that says New Outlook.

faq.question: Can I use custom keyboard shortcuts in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, you can assign them through System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts by entering the exact name of the menu command.

faq.question: What should I do if my Outlook search is not working?
faq.answer: Ensure your app is updated to the latest version. If the issue persists, try restarting the app or checking your internet connection.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with the new Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works in any app on your Mac, including the new Outlook interface, by helping you find buttons and dictate text.

faq.question: How do I add a shared mailbox in Outlook for Mac?
faq.answer: Go to File > Open > Shared Mailbox and enter the email address of the mailbox you want to add.
